attempts.label: DANDI:000713

inputs.what: Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework v3 annotation volume at 25 um (Wang et al. 2020) and its structure list, as packaged by BrainGlobe (allen_mouse_25um_v1.2.tar.gz, SHA-256 696276744cc6552e3be87b236498aebeb2de79be3b66ebffc1a620ee75a9c0a9, checked in the notebook), used for cortical layers and the CCF-derived area of the five layer claims.

The same CCFv3 2017 annotation volume at 25 um from the Allen Institute's download (annotation_25.nrrd, Last-Modified 2025-02-19, SHA-256 c620cbcc562183e4dcd40250d440130501781f74b41de35b1c1bdabace290c42) and the Allen structure ontology (structure_graph_download/1.json, SHA-256 b5f0d024d1df09ee18aef15093f55240f4a70b3924ee9689add612dadff80386), both checked in the notebook. Used in place of BrainGlobe's file when GIN refuses the request (it answered 403 Forbidden to the runner during the first revision), and loaded beside it when GIN answers, as in the final run, where the notebook shows that the two volumes (77,045,760 voxels) and structure lists are identical and give each of the 54,045 units the same area, layer and boundary distance. The paths carry no version, so the files are pinned by their hashes only.

attempts.entry_title: Reward coding across mouse visual cortical areas (Souza et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings on reward coding hold up in this data. Reward-modulated units are mostly suppressed, more in VISp than VISam and in narrow-spiking and layer 4 units, and their summed activity is less variable than the rest. Three results did not reproduce: how much better mixtures of response archetypes fit units than single ones, how little areas differ in them, and the variability change around image changes, for which the paper gives no windows. Some counts and controls, including those for layer 4, hold only in part or not. All results rest on an assumed choice of sessions and units, as the paper does not say which 103 of 153 sessions it used.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Souza et al. (2026) on dandiset 000713, the Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels dataset, which the paper reuses. It rebuilds the reward-modulated cohort of units in six visual areas (split-half test against an ISI-shuffle null, then two cross-condition contrasts), its composition by area and waveform class, the reward modulation index, the population variability of the cohort, the decomposition of peri-reward profiles into archetypes, and the behavioural numbers the paper reports. The layer analyses use the CCFv3 annotation volume as an outside input.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Souza et al. (2026) from dandiset 000713

outcomes.statement: The dandiset holds the data the paper analyzed, 103 sessions from 54 mice with 54,039 units in the six visual areas, with an active behavior block 0 and a passive replay block 5 in every session.
outcomes.quote: We analyzed extracellular recordings from 103 sessions of the Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels dataset (Bennett et al., 2026), acquired with Neuropixels 1.0 probes in 54 head-fixed trained adult mice ... yielding 54,039 units in total
outcomes.notes: Readings (a) and (b) of the criterion give 153 sessions from 81 mice, with 110,563 units in the six areas, or 45,354 with the Allen default thresholds; neither is within 10%. The 104 sessions of the 54 Sst-Cre and Vip-Cre mice, with units of quality good and presence ratio at least 0.95, give 104 sessions, 54 mice and 54,045 units (differences of 1, 0 and 6), within 10% but not exact; the other selections tried (quality good alone 66,388, Allen thresholds 30,705, all units 76,151 in those sessions) are further off. The files give no reason to leave out one of the 104 sessions; the smallest holds 262 units, so leaving out one session cannot give 54,039 units, and the one with the fewest hits (3) holds 903 units. The selection is used by every other claim. Open for the paper's authors, asked as a methods_unavailable finding.
deviations: The selection that fits (Sst-Cre and Vip-Cre mice, quality good, presence ratio at least 0.95) is not one of the criterion's two readings; it was found by comparing the counts of several selections with the paper's, and is adopted as an assumption.

outcomes.statement: Block 0 is the active behavior block and block 5 the passive replay block in all 103 sessions, and no lick or reward events occur during passive replay.
outcomes.quote: We verified this block assignment in all 103 sessions and confirmed that no lick or reward events occurred during passive replay
outcomes.notes: In all 104 sessions block 0 is the natural-image block with every presentation active and block 5 the same image sequence with none active; every trial lies within 1 s of block 0's bounds, every reward is in block 0, and no lick or reward time falls in block 5. The other blocks are spontaneous (1, 3), gabor (2) and flash (4) in every session.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).

outcomes.statement: Consecutive rewards are separated by at least 6.96 s, so no peri-reward window holds a neighboring reward.
outcomes.quote: Consecutive rewards were separated by at least 6.96 s in this dataset
outcomes.notes: The smallest interval between consecutive performance rewards is 6.972 s over the 104 sessions (per-session minima 6.97 to 46.84 s); with automatic rewards included it is the same. No session has an interval below 6.96 s.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).

outcomes.statement: Across sessions the median change-to-reward latency is 0.467 s; over 16,330 hit trials the median within-session standard deviation is 0.104 s (range 0.046 to 0.174 s), and 3.8% of hits depart from their session median by more than 250 ms.
outcomes.quote: Across sessions, the median change-to-reward latency was 0.467 s ... we quantified its within-session dispersion over the 16,330 hit trials ... the median within-session standard deviation was 0.104 s (range 0.046-0.174 s), and 3.8% of hits departed from their session median by more than 250 ms
outcomes.notes: With the change time from the trial table's change_time_no_display_delay, 15,592 hits, a median latency of 0.4507 s (median of session medians; pooled 0.4505), a median within-session SD of 0.1110 s (range 0.0464 to 0.1770 s, inside the widened range) are within tolerance, and 4.20% of hits depart from their session median by more than 250 ms, outside 3.42 to 4.18%. With the change presentation's start time (the displayed change), 0.4065 s and 4.31%, outside tolerance. The 15,592 hits are 738 fewer than the paper's 16,330; they are every hit trial of the 104 sessions (none auto-rewarded, without a reward time or change presentation, or with its window outside the block), and at the mean of 149.9 per session 103 sessions would hold 15,442.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).

Which time stands for the trial's image change is not given; the start of the change presentation and the trial table's change_time_no_display_delay (about 44 ms earlier) are both run. The criterion is met under neither.

outcomes.statement: Water is delivered a median of 9.8 ms after the nearest lick (95th percentile 17.3 ms, all within 20 ms), across the 16,330 earned rewards, so licking and reward cannot be separated by alignment.
outcomes.quote: across the 16,330 earned rewards of the 103 sessions, water was delivered a median of 9.8 ms after the nearest lick (95th percentile 17.3 ms, all within 20 ms)
outcomes.notes: Over the 15,592 earned rewards water follows the nearest lick by a median of 9.78 ms with a 95th percentile of 17.32 ms; the nearest lick always precedes the reward, so the two readings agree. 5 rewards come more than 22 ms after the nearest lick (maximum 53.5 ms), so not every delay is within 20 ms.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).

outcomes.statement: Of 54,039 units, 11,032 (20.4%; 32.9% of the 33,502 units testable in both contrasts) form the reward-modulated cohort, 7,229 suppressed (65.5%) and 3,803 enhanced (34.5%); 11,271 units were significant in both families, of which 239 had discordant signs.
outcomes.source: Results 3.1, paragraphs 2 and 3; Materials and methods 2.4, paragraph 4; Figure 1E
outcomes.quote: This cohort comprised 11,032 units out of the 54,039 recorded across the six visual areas (20.4%; 32.9% of the 33,502 units testable in both contrasts) ... Reward-suppressed units (7,229; 65.5% of the cohort) outnumbered reward-enhanced units (3,803; 34.5%) overall
outcomes.notes: Split-half positive 46,263 of 54,045 units (85.6%; 438 with r_split undefined). Family A significant 24,492, Family B 13,640, both 11,108, of which 286 discordant, leaving 10,822 (20.0% of tested), 7,378 suppressed (68.2%) and 3,444 enhanced (31.8%). Testable in both contrasts 34,959 under reading (a) (cohort 31.0% of it), 37,892 under (b), 45,785 under (c). All counts are within tolerance under reading (a) except the 286 discordant units (239, tolerance 24); per the criterion this is partially reproduced. 43,025 units are at the minimum p of 1/101; the BH threshold per area is 0.0396. The seed sensitivity of the null was not computed under the four further seeds (it needs the spike times again). With 1,000 permutations on 300 units of three sessions, 229 units have p at most 0.05 against 225 with 100 (224 under both). Reading (1b) of the null, over the whole recording, run on 12 of the 104 sessions (6,553 units, BH per area over them); cohort 1,268 against 1,272 under (1a), 1,266 in both (6 only under 1a, 2 only under 1b), 74 and 63 units split-half positive under only one reading, 19 discordant under each, suppressed 66.6% against 66.5%, so the outcome is the same under both readings.
deviations: The analysis uses the 104 sessions of the Sst-Cre and Vip-Cre mice and their units of quality good with presence ratio at least 0.95 in the six areas, the selection that fits the paper's counts (claim data-sessions-units); the paper does not say how its sessions and units were chosen, and its 103rd session could not be identified.

The ISI-shuffle null uses 100 permutations per unit, not the paper's 1,000 (M&M 2.3), as 1,000 for 54,045 units is about nine CPU hours, over the notebook limit; on 300 units of three sessions, 225 units have p at most 0.05 with 100 permutations and 229 with 1,000 (Spearman of the p values 0.913). The null rebuilds the train over the active block from its first spike (reading 1a of the criterion); the whole-recording reading (1b) takes over an hour for all sessions and was run on 12 of the 104.
Responsiveness uses the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with the normal approximation and tie correction for every trial count (scipy uses an exact test for 50 trials or fewer without ties or zeros).
Miss pseudo-reward time is the change plus the session median latency (reading 3, M&M 2.4). The trial's image change is the start of its change presentation in the block 0 stimulus table.
The session median latency for the pseudo-reward times uses the change presentation's start time (claim latency-change-to-reward).

outcomes.statement: The cohort's split-half reliabilities lie well above the ISI-shuffle null in all six areas.
outcomes.quote: both with near-ceiling reproducibility (rsplit ≈ 1.0) well above the null, which the full cohort exceeds (Figures 1C, D)
outcomes.notes: Per area the cohort's median r_split is 0.853 (VISrl) to 0.902 (VISp) against a pooled null median of 0.074 to 0.092 and a 95th percentile of 0.380 to 0.409 (null maximum 0.770 to 0.849); every cohort unit's r_split exceeds the median of its own null in every area (minimum r_split 0.255). Both readings hold. The pooled null has 100 values per unit. Reading (b) holds by construction, since a cohort unit passed the gate at p_split at most 0.0396, so at most 3 of its 100 null values reach its r_split; reading (a) carries the claim.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).
The paper gives no measure of well above; both readings in the criterion are run and agree.

The ISI-shuffle null uses 100 permutations per unit, not the paper's 1,000 (M&M 2.3), as 1,000 for 54,045 units is about nine CPU hours, over the notebook limit; on 300 units of three sessions, 225 units have p at most 0.05 with 100 permutations and 229 with 1,000 (Spearman of the p values 0.913). The null rebuilds the train over the active block from its first spike (reading 1a of the criterion); the whole-recording reading (1b) takes over an hour for all sessions and was run on 12 of the 104.

outcomes.statement: The cohort contains reward-enhanced units in VISam and reward-suppressed units in VISrl with near-ceiling split-half reproducibility (r_split 1.00 and 0.99 in the two examples).
outcomes.quote: Two example cells illustrate the two directions of modulation, one that increases its firing at reward (VISam) and one that decreases it (VISrl), both with near-ceiling reproducibility
outcomes.notes: Enhanced VISam cohort units 760, 8 with r_split at least 0.99 (maximum 0.9963); suppressed VISrl units 1,158, 32 with r_split at least 0.98 (maximum 0.9960). The paper's two example units are not identified, so they cannot be matched.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).

outcomes.statement: The per-unit suppressed fraction declines along the functional hierarchy, 86% in VISp (n = 2,374), 68% in VISl (1,782), 60% in VISrl (1,894), 61% in VISal (1,511), 59% in VISpm (1,765) and 51% in VISam (1,706), so the enhanced fraction rises from 14% in VISp to 49% in VISam.
outcomes.quote: Ordered along the functional visual hierarchy, the per-unit suppressed fraction was 86% in VISp (n = 2,374), 68% in VISl (n = 1,782), 60% in VISrl (n = 1,894), 61% in VISal (n = 1,511), 59% in VISpm (n = 1,765) and 51% in VISam (n = 1,706)
outcomes.notes: Suppressed fraction VISp 87.1% (2,108 of 2,421), VISl 70.3% (1,854 units), VISrl 62.6% (1,851), VISal 63.0% (1,447), VISpm 63.3% (1,612), VISam 53.6% (1,637), all within tolerance; VISp highest and VISam lowest. VISp exceeds VISam in 45 of the 54 mice. The per-area n of VISl, VISrl, VISal and VISpm are within 5, 2, 4 and 9% of the paper's.

outcomes.statement: With the session as the unit of analysis, the median suppressed fraction falls from 0.92 in VISp to 0.52 in VISam and the areas differ (Kruskal-Wallis, p < 0.001).
outcomes.quote: with the recording session as the unit of analysis, the per-session median suppressed fraction fell from 0.92 in VISp to 0.52 in VISam, and the areas differed (Kruskal-Wallis, p < 0.001; Figure 1L)

statistics.test: Kruskal-Wallis test across the six areas
statistics.n: sessions with at least five cohort units in an area

outcomes.notes: With at least five cohort units per session and area (91 VISp, 88 VISam sessions), the median suppressed fraction is 0.911 in VISp and 0.575 in VISam; VISam is 0.003 outside tolerance (0.468 to 0.572). Kruskal-Wallis H = 86.4, p = 3.8e-17 across the six areas.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).

outcomes.statement: Drawing pseudo-reward latencies at random from each session's hit latencies, twenty times, leaves 99.2% of the cohort passing Family A with unchanged SI sign (range 99.1 to 99.3%), and the index correlates with its original value at rho = 0.996.
outcomes.quote: across the twenty realizations, 99.2% of the cohort continued to pass Family A with an unchanged sign of the specificity index (range 99.1-99.3%) and the index correlated with its original value at ρ = 0.996
outcomes.notes: Over the twenty realizations 99.14% of the cohort (98.97 to 99.23%) passes Family A again with the same SI sign; Spearman rho of the jittered SI with the original 0.9959 (0.9953 to 0.9964), Pearson 0.9995. The jitter draws use the claim's seed plus the session index; the four further seeds were not run, as they need the spike times again, and the twenty realizations all give values within tolerance.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).
Seed sensitivity under the claim's seed plus 1000 to 4000 was not computed.

outcomes.statement: The two-component Gaussian mixture on trough-to-peak duration labels 849 of 53,806 units (1.6%) ambiguous, 227 of them in the cohort (2.1%); widening the band to 0.3 to 0.7 removes 1,280 units (2.4%) and leaves the suppressed fractions at 0.790 in narrow and 0.617 in broad units, against 0.790 and 0.619 with the 0.4 to 0.6 band.
outcomes.quote: this removed 849 of 53,806 units (1.6%), of which 227 belonged to the cohort (2.1% of it). Widening the ambiguous band to 0.3-0.7 removed 1,280 units (2.4%) and left the results unchanged
outcomes.notes: 54,045 units enter the fit (all have a duration; expected 53,806). Reading (b), the stored waveform_duration, components at 0.264 and 0.621 ms, the same under all five seeds; ambiguous 405 (0.75%) with the band 0.4 to 0.6, 110 of them in the cohort (1.02%), and 1,205 with 0.3 to 0.7, which alone is within tolerance. Reading (a), duration on the stored 30 kHz mean waveform (60 distinct values, 1st to 99th percentile 0.200 to 1.433 ms), components at 0.534 and 0.616 ms under the claim's seed and the seed plus 1000, and 0.57 and 1.425 ms under the other three seeds; 1,292 ambiguous, 245 in the cohort, 6,510 with the wide band. The claim's seed gives the higher log-likelihood (24,671 against 19,781), so the degenerate split is the better fit, not a failed one. The waveform rows are laid out as assumed; every unit has 384 rows and in 230 of 300 units checked the largest-amplitude row is the peak channel's (299 within 4 channels). Upsampled to 200 points (a variant), 97.5% of durations are within 0.02 ms of the stored ones, but 1,263 units are more than 0.1 ms away (median 1.421 against 0.371 ms) and the mixture again puts a component on that tail (0.571 and 1.491 ms, 34 ambiguous). The suppressed fractions of the statement are judged in claim narrow-more-suppressed.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).
Reading (a) measures trough to the following maximum on the peak channel's mean waveform at its stored 30 kHz sampling, without upsampling; the paper does not say whether it upsampled.

outcomes.statement: The narrow-spiking fraction of the cohort is highest in VISp and VISrl (about 26%) and lower in the other four areas (14 to 19%).
outcomes.quote: The narrow fraction was highest in VISp and VISrl (approximately 26%) and lower in the remaining areas (14-19%; Figures 1J, K)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a) of the fraction (narrow among narrow and broad cohort units), stored duration; VISp 25.0%, VISrl 27.1%, VISl 19.2%, VISal 20.1%, VISpm 15.2%, VISam 16.5%. Within suppressed units 18.6 to 32.5%, within enhanced 7.7 to 18.1%. With durations from the mean waveform the fractions are 28.5 to 44.2%.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).

Waveform classes are judged on the units table's waveform_duration (reading b of claim waveform-ambiguous-band); the mixture on durations from the 30 kHz mean waveform does not separate narrow and broad units.

outcomes.statement: Median ISI is lower in narrow-spiking cohort units (40.9 ms, n = 2,308) than in broad-spiking units (85.0 ms, n = 8,716).
outcomes.quote: Median ISI was lower in narrow-spiking (40.9 ms, n = 2,308) than in broad-spiking units (85.0 ms, n = 8,716)
outcomes.notes: Stored duration, ambiguous units excluded, whole recording; narrow 42.2 ms (2,245 units), broad 88.0 ms (8,467). With the active block only 47.2 and 89.9 ms; with classes by the larger posterior 2,355 narrow units (43.3 ms). The paper's 11,024 classified units exceed its 10,805 cohort units left after the ambiguous ones; 2,245 plus 8,467 is 10,712 here.

Waveform classes are judged on the units table's waveform_duration (reading b of claim waveform-ambiguous-band); the mixture on durations from the 30 kHz mean waveform does not separate narrow and broad units.

outcomes.quote: a separation that also held in complementary metrics of waveform shape (half-width) and of spiking statistics (median inter-spike interval and autocorrelogram rise time; Figures 1G-I, O)

Waveform classes are judged on the units table's waveform_duration (reading b of claim waveform-ambiguous-band); the mixture on durations from the 30 kHz mean waveform does not separate narrow and broad units.

outcomes.source: Materials and methods 2.5, paragraph 1; Results 3.2, paragraph 4

outcomes.quote: Second, narrow-spiking units were more frequently suppressed than broad-spiking units, and this difference persisted within each layer (85% of sessions; p < 0.001)

Reading (b), 80.2% of 172 session and layer pairs, p = 4.8e-18. With durations from the mean waveform 73.9% (p = 4.6e-06) and 63.1%.

outcomes.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 3; Figures 1M and 1N; Materials and methods 2.5, paragraph 4

outcomes.notes: Smoothed histogram; cohort median M -0.1743, 75.3% with M < 0, per-area medians VISp -0.2773, VISl -0.1947, VISrl -0.1109, VISal -0.1448, VISpm -0.1619, VISam -0.1282, all negative. Unsmoothed -0.1757 and 75.2%. The median is outside tolerance (-0.1455 to -0.1191); the fraction and the signs hold.

outcomes.statement: Moving the M baseline to -1.5 to -1.0 s raises the median M from -0.1323 to -0.0351 and lowers the fraction with M < 0 from 71.6% to 54.5%; the median changes sign in VISal, VISpm and VISam, VISp stays the most negative under every baseline, and 44.6% of reward-enhanced units have negative M under the adjacent baseline against 1.9% under the retreated one.
outcomes.source: Materials and methods 2.5, paragraph 4 (beginning "The pre-reward baseline is deliberately adjacent"); Discussion, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Retreating the baseline to -1.5 to -1.0 s raises the median M from -0.1323 to -0.0351 and lowers the fraction of units with M < 0 from 71.6% to 54.5%, with the median changing sign in VISal, VISpm and VISam; the ordering across areas is preserved, VISp being the most negative under every baseline tested
outcomes.notes: Smoothed; baseline -1.5 to -1.0 s gives a median M of -0.0413 (outside -0.0386 to -0.0316), 55.9% with M < 0 (within), and 2.41% of enhanced units with M < 0 (outside 1.71 to 2.09); 42.7% of enhanced units have M < 0 with the adjacent baseline (within). Under -1.5 to -1.0 s the medians are VISal +0.0020, VISpm -0.0021, VISam +0.0377 and VISp -0.0825; VISpm does not change sign. VISp is the most negative under all four baselines (-0.2773, -0.0894, -0.0825, -0.1728). No reward's -2.0 s baseline starts before the block.

outcomes.statement: A layer is assigned to 87.5% of the 54,039 units and 84.9% of the cohort, from 96.6% in VISam to 48.0% in VISrl, and the CCF-derived area agrees with the unit-table label for 63.5% of tested units.
outcomes.quote: A layer was assigned to 87.5% of the 54,039 tested units and to 84.9% of the cohort, ranging from 96.6% in VISam to 48.0% in VISrl, and the CCF-derived area agreed with the unit-table label for 63.5% of tested units
outcomes.notes: Layer assigned to 97.2% of the 54,045 tested units and 97.3% of the cohort; by area 96.5 to 98.5% of all units (VISam 96.5%, VISrl 97.4%) and 95.8 to 98.1% of the cohort (VISam 95.8%, VISrl 97.5%). 1,508 units have a CCF coordinate of 0 or below and no layer. The CCF-derived area equals the unit-table label for 66.0% of tested units, within tolerance; disagreements are mostly VISli (4,513) and SSp-bfd (3,735). The paper's 48.0% in VISrl is not approached under either reading. A stricter rule outside the criterion, a layer only where the CCF structure is a visual area, gives 87.0% of tested units, 84.3% of the cohort, 96.5% in VISam and 45.5% in VISrl, all within tolerance, which suggests the paper used such a rule; its Methods do not state it, so it is asked of the authors (methods_unavailable finding) and the outcome stays on the criterion's rule. No unit falls in a CCF structure whose acronym ends in a layer suffix without being laminar (such as CA1), so the guard added for that changes nothing.
deviations: Sessions and units as claim data-sessions-units finds them (an assumption).

The annotation volume is the CCFv3 2017 annotation at 25 um (Wang et al. 2020), as BrainGlobe's allen_mouse_25um v1.2 packages it or, when GIN refuses the request, from the Allen Institute's download; in the final run both were loaded, and their volumes, structure lists and the layers of all 54,045 units are identical. The paper names no release. Unit coordinates are the electrodes table's x, y, z of the peak channel, rounded to the nearest 25 um voxel.

outcomes.statement: Among units with an assigned layer, suppression is concentrated in layer 4; the per-session suppressed fraction is higher there than in the other layers in 70 of 87 sessions (80%), by a median of +0.116 (IQR +0.04 to +0.20; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank, p < 0.001).

findings.statement: 1,508 of the 54,045 analysed units (quality good, presence ratio at least 0.95, in the six visual areas) have a CCF coordinate (electrodes table x, y or z) of 0 or below, a value that falls outside the brain; the files do not say that 0 marks a missing registration, while these units still carry an area label in the location column.

The units table's waveform_duration and the trough-to-peak duration measured on the stored mean waveform of the peak channel agree only at r = 0.66 (median difference -0.004 ms). The stored mean waveforms are sampled at 30 kHz (82 samples), so their durations take 60 distinct values and a two-component mixture on them does not separate narrow from broad units, while the stored waveform_duration (151 values) does; the files do not say how waveform_duration was computed. Upsampled to 200 points, the measured durations agree with the stored ones within 0.02 ms for 97.5% of units, but 1,263 units differ by more than 0.1 ms (median 1.421 against 0.371 ms).

Checks that passed. In all 104 sessions analysed, block 0 is the active natural-image block and block 5 its passive replay with the same image sequence and no licks or rewards; water follows the nearest lick by 1.3 to 53.5 ms (median 9.78 ms), so rewards and licks share a clock; and the summed spiking of each session's units rises after the image changes of the stimulus table (post to pre ratio 1.19 to 4.12, against 0.52 to 1.29 with the times shifted 0.25 s), so spikes and stimuli share a clock.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook of the first run with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier checked the archive's session and subject counts and tested the helpers on synthetic data. It gave its own outcome for all 38 claims (17 reproduced, 10 partially reproduced, 11 not reproduced) and disagreed with five. It reported no place where the claims file misreads the paper, so no question was added for a reader. Report in transcripts/souza-2026/verifier-1-report.md.

disagreements.reason: Under the criterion's readings (a) and (b), cell 5 gives 153 sessions / 81 mice / 110,563 or 45,354 units, more than 10% off all three counts. The archive API agrees; 153 session files, 81 subjects. The notebook's own selection (Sst/Vip mice, good, presence ratio at least 0.95) gives 104 / 54 / 54,045; close, but not exact and not a reading the criterion lists.

Cell 17. Using change-presentation times, median 0.4065 s (outside 0.467 plus or minus 0.047) and 4.31% of hits beyond 250 ms (outside 3.8 plus or minus 0.38). Using change_time_no_display_delay, median 0.451 within, but 4.20% still outside. Hits 15,592 (within tolerance) and SD 0.111 (within) under both.

Cell 50, baseline -1.5 to -1.0 s; median -0.041 (outside -0.0351 plus or minus 0.0035); enhanced units with M < 0 2.4% (outside 1.9 plus or minus 0.19); VISpm median stays negative (-0.002). VISp is the most negative area under all four baselines.
Cell 58; under every reading, at least one excess and the 6a narrow percentage are outside tolerance. Duration (a) narrow p = 1e-5, which misses p < 1e-6.

Cell 60; rate-matched +0.125 (against 0.178), unmatched +0.122 (against 0.148), at least 50 um +0.142 (against 0.176), and 80 sessions (against 72) are all outside tolerance. The partial clause's 50 um count therefore fails as well. Problem 7; denominator (b) uses test_a, which already requires a split-half positive unit, so the detection rate is 100% / 100%.

disagreements.reason: The criterion allows the 10% partial outcome for its own readings (a) and (b). Under both, the counts are more than 10% off (cell 5; 153 sessions / 81 mice / 110,563 or 45,354 units). The Sst/Vip, good, presence ratio at least 0.95 selection is not one of those readings. If protocol step 1.6 says what the response quotes, the author's choice is defensible. The disagreement is recorded and changes no other outcome. The assumption is stated and reasonable.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the paper's authors. Which 103 sessions and which units were analysed? The dandiset version holds 153 sessions from 81 mice. The 104 sessions of the Sst-Cre and Vip-Cre mice, with units of quality good and presence ratio at least 0.95 in the six areas, give 104 sessions, 54 mice and 54,045 units, close to the paper's 103, 54 and 54,039; was this the selection, and which session was left out? Every outcome of this attempt rests on the assumption.

Question for the paper's authors. How were the peak time of an archetype (Figure 3A) and the sign of a unit's pre against post-reward ramp (Figure 3D) defined? Peaks as the maximum absolute value of the signed archetype fit the paper's six roles; peaks as the signed maximum do not. Mean responses over -0.5 to 0 against 0 to 1.5 s match the anticipatory fractions; 0 to 0.5 s and the archetype weights do not.

Question for the paper's authors. How was a lick bout defined (Discussion, paragraph 7), and did the ISI-shuffle null rebuild the spike train over the active block or the whole recording? Bouts split at 500 ms gaps give the paper's 415 bouts per session (438 here); 250 ms gives 737. The null was run over the active block only.

The paper's counts do not add up in two places. The Figure 1H legend classifies 2,308 narrow and 8,716 broad cohort units, 11,024, more than the 10,805 cohort units left after the 227 ambiguous ones (Materials and methods 2.5). The unmatched layer-4 excess in the rate-matching control is +0.148, against +0.116 for the same comparison in the preceding sentence (Results 3.2); here both are about +0.12.

The paper states that it analysed 103 sessions from 54 mice but not how they were chosen from the dandiset's 153 sessions from 81 mice, nor which units entered (54,039 of 110,563 units in the six areas). The counts fit the Sst-Cre and Vip-Cre mice and units with quality good and presence ratio at least 0.95.

Question for the paper's authors. Were cortical layers assigned only where the CCF structure at the unit's coordinates is a visual area? Assigning a layer in any laminar CCF structure, as Materials and methods 2.5 reads, gives 97.2% of tested units and 97.4% in VISrl; keeping only visual-area structures gives 87.0%, 84.3% of the cohort, 96.5% in VISam and 45.5% in VISrl, close to the paper's 87.5%, 84.9%, 96.6% and 48.0%.

entries.name: souza-2026
entries.title: Reward coding across mouse visual cortical areas (Souza et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Souza et al. (2026) on dandiset 000713, the Allen Visual Behavior Neuropixels dataset, which the paper reuses. It rebuilds the reward-modulated cohort of units in six visual areas (split-half test against an ISI-shuffle null, then two cross-condition contrasts), its composition by area and waveform class, the reward modulation index, the population variability of the cohort, the decomposition of peri-reward profiles into archetypes, and the behavioural numbers the paper reports. The layer analyses use the CCFv3 annotation volume as an outside input.
